newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees $350 million oil deficit in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees $350 million oil deficit in 1996.

text.p: Peru Energy and Mines Minister Daniel Hokama predicted Peru would register a $350 million oil and derivatives trade deficit in 1996.
Hokama told foreign reporters this was a rise from $300 million in 1995, but previous official ministry figures had put last year's total at $323.2 million.
He added the government was negotiating with four foreign oil companies for new contracts to explore in Peru's jungle region.
Hokama named these companies as OXY, Advantage International, Phillip Petroleum and a consortium of Shell and Mobil.
The energy ministry had previously said in August it hoped to awared around 10 more exploration contracts before the end of the year.
Hokama said the projected oil trade deficit for this year was a record figure. "The only way to recover the equilibrium is to discover new oil fields," he said.

Latest ministry figures show Peru's oil trade deficit up 14.7 percent in the first half, compared with the same period last year, to $148 million. In the first six months, imports of oil and derivatives rose 37 percent to $334 million, while exports rose 63 percent to $186 million, compared with the same period in 1995.
Hokama added that the mining sector accounted for about $3 billion of Peru's estimated total Gross Domestic Product this year of around $62 billion.
In a suprise cabinet change by President Alberto Fujimori, Hokama was named soon after 1300 local/1800 GMT to the vacant post of presidency minister.
No replacement was named at the energy and mines ministry.
